datasets.name: city_totals
queryLines:
SELECT city, listings, active_listings, pct_active, hosts, round(listings / hosts, 2) AS listings_per_host,
       pct_multi_listing_hosts, median_price, p25_price, p75_price, median_availability_365, pct_closed_all_year,
       avg_review_rating, pct_with_reviews, pct_superhost
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.city_metrics_all
WHERE room_type = 'All'
ORDER BY CASE city WHEN 'Geneva' THEN 1 WHEN 'Zurich' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

datasets.name: room_mix
queryLines:
SELECT city, room_type, listings, pct_of_listings, median_price
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.city_metrics_all
WHERE room_type <> 'All'

datasets.name: neighbourhoods
queryLines:
SELECT city, neighbourhood, listings, priced_listings, median_price, pct_entire_home,
       row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY listings DESC) AS size_rank
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.neighbourhood_metrics_all
QUALIFY size_rank <= 15

datasets.name: price_bands
queryLines:
WITH b AS (
  SELECT city, CASE WHEN price < 50 THEN '0-49' WHEN price < 100 THEN '50-99' WHEN price < 150 THEN '100-149'
                    WHEN price < 200 THEN '150-199' WHEN price < 300 THEN '200-299' WHEN price < 500 THEN '300-499'
                    ELSE '500+' END AS price_band,
         CASE WHEN price < 50 THEN 1 WHEN price < 100 THEN 2 WHEN price < 150 THEN 3 WHEN price < 200 THEN 4
              WHEN price < 300 THEN 5 WHEN price < 500 THEN 6 ELSE 7 END AS band_order
  FROM workspace.ga2_gold.listings_all WHERE has_price AND outlier_class <> 'implausible'
)
SELECT city, concat(band_order, ') ', price_band) AS price_band,
       round(100 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY city), 1) AS pct_of_listings
FROM b GROUP BY city, band_order, price_band

datasets.name: ab_compare
queryLines:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT * FROM workspace.ga2_gold.city_metrics_all WHERE room_type = 'All' AND city IN ('Geneva', 'Zurich')
), long AS (
  SELECT city, stack(10,
    1, 'Listings', CAST(listings AS DOUBLE),
    2, 'Active listings (%)', pct_active,
    3, 'Hosts', CAST(hosts AS DOUBLE),
    4, 'Listings per host', listings / hosts,
    5, 'Median price (CHF)', median_price,
    6, 'Median availability (days / year)', CAST(median_availability_365 AS DOUBLE),
    7, 'Closed all year (%)', pct_closed_all_year,
    8, 'Average review score', avg_review_rating,
    9, 'With reviews (%)', pct_with_reviews,
    10, 'Superhosts (%)', pct_superhost
  ) AS (ord, metric, value)
  FROM m
)
SELECT ord, metric,
       round(max(CASE WHEN city = 'Geneva' THEN value END), 2) AS geneva,
       round(max(CASE WHEN city = 'Zurich' THEN value END), 2) AS zurich,
       round(100 * (max(CASE WHEN city = 'Zurich' THEN value END) / max(CASE WHEN city = 'Geneva' THEN value END) - 1), 1)
         AS zurich_vs_geneva_pct
FROM long GROUP BY ord, metric ORDER BY ord

datasets.name: ab_room_price
queryLines:
SELECT city, room_type, median_price, listings
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.city_metrics_all
WHERE city IN ('Geneva', 'Zurich') AND room_type IN ('Entire home/apt', 'Private room')

datasets.name: ab_like_for_like
queryLines:
SELECT city, room_type, CAST(accommodates AS STRING) AS guests, count(*) AS listings,
       round(percentile(price, 0.5), 1) AS median_price
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.listings_all
WHERE has_price AND outlier_class <> 'implausible' AND city IN ('Geneva', 'Zurich') AND room_type = 'Entire home/apt' AND accommodates BETWEEN 1 AND 6
GROUP BY ALL

datasets.name: ab_size
queryLines:
SELECT city, CASE WHEN accommodates >= 6 THEN '6+' ELSE CAST(accommodates AS STRING) END AS guests,
       round(100 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY city), 1) AS pct_of_listings
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.listings_all
WHERE has_price AND outlier_class <> 'implausible' AND city IN ('Geneva', 'Zurich')
GROUP BY ALL

datasets.name: mae_by_city
queryLines:
WITH ev AS (
  SELECT CASE city WHEN 'Geneva' THEN '1 Geneva (A)' WHEN 'Zurich' THEN '2 Zurich (B)' ELSE '3 A + B' END AS city_label,
         baseline_mae, model_mae
  FROM workspace.ga2_gold.model_evaluation
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CASE run WHEN 'first_run' THEN '4 Vaud (C), first run' ELSE '5 Vaud (C), after changes' END,
         baseline_mae_c, model_mae_c
  FROM workspace.ga2_gold.city_c_report WHERE rows = 'test'
)
SELECT city_label, 'Baseline' AS method, baseline_mae AS mae FROM ev
UNION ALL
SELECT city_label, 'Model', model_mae FROM ev

datasets.name: test_predictions
queryLines:
SELECT city, room_type, neighbourhood, name, listing_url, price, predicted_price, baseline_price,
       error, abs_error, baseline_abs_error, pct_error
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.predictions_all
WHERE label_ok AND split = 'test'

datasets.name: mae_by_room_type
queryLines:
SELECT city, room_type, count(*) AS test_listings, round(avg(abs_error), 1) AS model_mae,
       round(avg(baseline_abs_error), 1) AS baseline_mae
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.predictions_all
WHERE label_ok AND split = 'test'
GROUP BY ALL
HAVING count(*) >= 20

datasets.name: mae_by_neighbourhood
queryLines:
SELECT concat(neighbourhood, ' (', city, ')') AS area, city, count(*) AS test_listings,
       round(avg(abs_error), 1) AS model_mae, round(avg(baseline_abs_error), 1) AS baseline_mae,
       round(percentile(pct_error, 0.5), 1) AS median_pct_error
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.predictions_all
WHERE label_ok AND split = 'test'
GROUP BY ALL
HAVING count(*) >= 15

datasets.name: extremes
queryLines:
SELECT city, CASE WHEN error > 0 THEN 'over-priced' ELSE 'under-priced' END AS direction,
       name, neighbourhood, room_type, accommodates, price, predicted_price, error, pct_error, listing_url,
       row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY city, error > 0 ORDER BY abs(error) DESC) AS rank
FROM workspace.ga2_gold.predictions_all
WHERE label_ok AND split = 'test' AND error <> 0
QUALIFY rank <= 10
ORDER BY city, direction, rank

datasets.name: vaud_steps
queryLines:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT CASE step WHEN 0 THEN '1 first run' WHEN 1 THEN '2 + city level' ELSE '3 + municipality level' END AS step,
         model_mae_c, baseline_mae_c
  FROM workspace.ga2_gold.city_c_changes
)
SELECT step, 'Model' AS method, model_mae_c AS mae FROM c
UNION ALL
SELECT step, 'Baseline', baseline_mae_c FROM c

datasets.name: vaud_areas
queryLines:
WITH top AS (
  SELECT neighbourhood FROM workspace.ga2_gold.predictions_after_change_vaud GROUP BY neighbourhood ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 8
), p AS (
  SELECT neighbourhood, price, price_first_run, price_city_level, price_area_level
  FROM workspace.ga2_gold.predictions_after_change_vaud WHERE neighbourhood IN (SELECT neighbourhood FROM top)
)
SELECT neighbourhood, '1 first run' AS step, round(percentile(100 * (price_first_run - price) / price, 0.5), 1) AS median_pct_error, count(*) AS test_listings FROM p GROUP BY neighbourhood
UNION ALL
SELECT neighbourhood, '2 + city level', round(percentile(100 * (price_city_level - price) / price, 0.5), 1), count(*) FROM p GROUP BY neighbourhood
UNION ALL
SELECT neighbourhood, '3 + municipality level', round(percentile(100 * (price_area_level - price) / price, 0.5), 1), count(*) FROM p GROUP BY neighbourhood

## Entire homes make up 70-76% of listings in every city, and about a third of all listings are inactive

Geneva (A), Zurich (B) and Vaud (C), Inside Airbnb snapshots of Sep-Oct 2026. Prices in CHF per night; price figures use only listings with a usable price (inactive listings and 14 implausible prices excluded).

frame.title: Vaud has the most listings; Zurich is the most expensive and the least available
frame.description: One row per city, from city_metrics_all where room_type = 'All' (never a sum of room types).

frame.title: Entire homes dominate everywhere; private rooms are 24-30%
An entire home costs 1.7-2.2 times a private room
Vaud has the longest expensive tail: 20% of its listings ask CHF 300 or more (Geneva 12%, Zurich 18%)
frame.description: Share of each city's listings with a usable price, per price band.

lines: Vaud's neighbourhoods are municipalities: Lausanne is cheaper than the resorts (Ollon, Gryon, Montreux).

## Zurich is 20% pricier per night than Geneva, but only 8-11% for a same-size flat: Zurich listings are bigger

City A = Geneva, city B = Zurich. Median prices in CHF per night, listings with a usable price.

frame.title: Zurich: higher prices, 28% fewer open days, more listings per host and superhosts
frame.description: City totals (room_type = 'All'). Last column: how much higher (+) or lower (-) Zurich is.

frame.title: The gap is in entire homes (+15%); private rooms differ by 6%
Same number of guests, much smaller gap: entire homes for 2 guests +8%, for 4 guests +11%
Zurich has more listings for 4+ guests, which lifts its city-wide median

lines:
## The model beats the baseline by 20% on Geneva and Zurich and by 19% on Vaud after the changes; its largest errors are in the Vaud Alps

Every number is on the test set (20% of listings per city, never used for training or model choice). Baseline = median training price for the same room type and number of guests. error = predicted - actual: positive = the model over-prices. Vaud rows in the charts below are the **first run** (unchanged week 1 model); the changes are shown at the bottom.

frame.title: Model vs baseline: lower is better
frame.description: Vaud is harder for any method: its baseline error is 19% higher than on A + B.

frame.title: Predicted vs actual price: points above the diagonal are over-priced
frame.description: Test listings. The model is pulled towards the middle: cheap listings are over-priced, expensive ones under-priced.

frame.title: Entire homes carry the largest errors in CHF
frame.description: Room types with at least 20 test listings.

frame.title: Alpine municipalities (Ormont-Dessous, Gryon, Château-d'Oex) have the largest errors; Lausanne and Zurich's residential districts the smallest
frame.description: Neighbourhoods with at least 15 test listings.

frame.title: The 10 most over- and under-priced test listings per city
frame.description: Under-priced (error < 0): the model suggests less than the host asks. Over-priced: more.

lines:
## Vaud (city C): the municipality price level removed the bias the first run had

Change 1: one city-free model plus a price level for the city, learnt from Vaud's known (train) prices. Change 2: plus a price level per municipality, shrunk to 0 where few prices are known.

frame.title: Vaud MAE: 71.9 first run, 70.6 with a city level, 68.1 with municipality levels (baseline 84.0)
Lausanne went from 21% over-priced to -4%; Montreux from -12% to 0%
frame.description: The 8 Vaud municipalities with the most test listings.
